content.text:
Confirmed the underlying issue on Apple silicon with rustc 1.97.1.

A minimal proc macro built in two directories with source-path remapping produced:

| Link configuration | Differing bytes |
|---|---:|
| Default install name | 48 |
| Stable `@rpath/libaudit_macro.dylib` install name | 0 |

Both stable outputs passed code-signature verification and successfully compiled and ran a consumer using the macro.

The [reported cascade](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/discussions/419#discussioncomment-18391765) matches current mbx code: verification leaves the freshly compiled dylib in place, and dependents hash its exact bytes. Changing those bytes changes their cache keys. I haven’t independently reproduced the full 39-miss workload.

**I recommend stabilizing the install name at link time for macOS proc macros.** The experiment used `-C link-arg=-Wl,-install_name,@rpath/libaudit_macro.dylib`. That also made the UUID and signature identical, preserving strict verification and content hashing.

Rewriting on restore would still produce checkout-specific bytes. Ignoring Mach-O fields in dependency hashes would require a broader equivalence contract, particularly for ordinary dylibs where install names matter.

An implementation should derive the name per output, respect explicit linker settings, and distinguish the changed compilation policy in cache keys. No repository changes or GitHub replies made.

I’ll implement stable install names for macOS proc macros, validate the change, and open a PR. Then I’ll reply to the discussion with the findings and PR link.
